hero.headline: Oil nears $97 after reported mine hits on two tankers and a strike on a Saudi refinery.
hero.dek: Every story on FIOPO is traced to where it lands: your fuel, your rent, your savings, your job. Here is how today's biggest story travels.

chain.label: The event
chain.text: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on November 26 that two oil tankers hit naval mines and caught fire north of Oman's port of Khasab in the Strait of Hormuz. It said one was a supertanker carrying more than 2 million barrels. The account comes from the IRGC and was reported by Iran International.

chain.label: The second hit
chain.text: The same day, Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry said a hostile aerial projectile hit the Jazan refinery, which can process up to 400,000 barrels a day, starting a fire and suspending some operations. One Nepali worker was killed and several others were injured, Arab News reports.

chain.label: The price
chain.text: Brent rose 0.77% to $97.31 a barrel in Asian trade on Friday and US crude rose 2.99% to $86.18, AP reports. Brent settled Thursday at its highest since November 6. On Wednesday Brent closed at $90.82.

chain.label: The ripple
chain.text: India, a big oil importer, felt it first: the Sensex fell 989.33 points to 83,339.26 on Friday and the rupee weakened to about 92.98 per dollar, with rising crude the main drag, IANS reports. ANZ says Brent can push above $100 even without another major escalation.

chain.label: You
chain.text: US gas averaged $3.56 on November 26, down from $3.72 a week earlier, AAA says. Higher crude, if it lasts, could slow that decline. OPEC+ meets Sunday to set 2027 output policy.

hero.caption: Sources: Iran International, Arab News, AP, Wisevoter citing FXEmpire, PiQ Markets, IANS and AAA, November 26 to 27, 2026. The chain itself is FIOPO analysis.

stories.headline: Asian stocks rally and US futures rise before Wall Street's Black Friday half day.
stories.happened: On Thursday, with US markets shut for Thanksgiving, Europe's STOXX 600 closed up 1.8% at 636.98, Germany's DAX rose 2.1% to 25,215.52 and France's CAC 40 rose 1.6% to 8,108.74, JBizNews reports. On Friday Japan's Nikkei 225 rose about 2.0% to 58,628.59, South Korea's KOSPI 4.2% to 4,906.93 and the Shanghai Composite 3.2% to 3,586.30 in AP's midday count.
stories.happening: Hong Kong's Hang Seng closed up 2.11% at 22,694.77 and its tech index jumped 6.45% after a State Council meeting discussed stabilizing China's capital market, Longbridge reports. US stock futures were up about 0.7% for the S&P 500 overnight, IC Markets says. US markets close at 1 p.m. ET on Friday. Adobe forecasts $12.9 billion in US online Black Friday spending, up 9.2%.

could.text: A rebound across Asia and Europe after a volatile week is meeting a short, thin US session, which can exaggerate moves either way.

you: Avoid market orders in Friday's short session, when trading is thin and prices can jump.
Check how much of your fund sits in Asian and European stocks; they led this week's rebound.
Shopping Black Friday deals? Compare the price with the past month's history before you buy; Salesforce says November discounts are 8% bigger than last year.
stories.watch: The US session closing at 1 p.m. ET Friday.

stories.headline: Oil climbs as Iran's IRGC says two tankers hit mines in Hormuz and a strike shuts part of a Saudi refinery.
stories.happened: Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy said on November 26 that two oil tankers hit naval mines and caught fire north of Khasab, Oman, while using what it called an unauthorized route. It said one was a supertanker with more than 2 million barrels aboard. No tanker names were given. The same day Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry said a projectile hit Aramco's Jazan refinery, killing a Nepali worker and suspending some operations. Arab News attributes the attack to the Houthis.
stories.happening: Brent traded at $97.31 on Friday, up 0.77%, and US crude at $86.18, up 2.99%, AP reports. On Wednesday Brent closed at $90.82 and WTI at $84.15, Globicus says. Oil is set for its first weekly gain after a string of losses. OPEC+ meets Sunday to set 2027 output; Iraq and Kazakhstan are pressing for higher capacity estimates, Wisevoter reports. The Saudi led coalition said it destroyed a missile launch platform at Hodeidah port.

odds.label: Brent at or above $100 on Dec 27

could.note: FIOPO read for the next 30 days, given repeated attacks on Gulf energy sites and the OPEC+ decision. Judgment, not fact.

you: Driving this weekend? Fill up where prices are posted lowest; the US average was $3.56 on November 26, AAA says.
Heat with heating oil or propane? Compare suppliers now, since oil price jumps reach heating fuel quickly.
Flying in the Gulf region? Check your airline's updates; Al Jazeera reports most international flights to Riyadh are cancelled.
stories.watch: The OPEC+ meeting on Sunday, November 29.

sources.name: AP via Click2Houston, Asian markets, Nov 27

stories.headline: Altria says it may make a cash offer for Imperial Brands, and Imperial's shares jump 13.3%.
stories.happened: On November 26 Altria, the Marlboro maker in the US, said it is considering a possible offer for Britain's Imperial Brands that would likely be solely in cash, and that it is talking with a third party about buying part of Imperial's business. Imperial said it has had no discussions with and received no approach from Altria or the third party. Imperial shares rose 13.3% to 3,432 pence, their highest close since July 2017, Investing.com reports.
stories.happening: Bloomberg reported that Japan Tobacco has explored partnering with another buyer and splitting Imperial's assets by region, at an early stage, Investing.com says. Japan Tobacco shares closed up 4.5% on Friday against a 1.7% rise in the TOPIX, Reuters reports. Imperial is valued at £25.90 billion ($34 billion), and Altria had $2.7 billion in cash at the end of September. Under UK takeover rules Altria must make a firm offer or walk away by 5 p.m. on December 24.

could.text: A deal of this size would be the largest takeover of a listed UK company in more than eight years, but nothing has been offered yet.

you: Own Imperial shares? Imperial has told shareholders to take no action for now.
Hold Altria for its dividend? Watch Friday's first US trade on the news and any detail on how a deal would be paid for.
Hold a UK or global dividend fund? Check whether Imperial is a large holding after the jump.
stories.watch: Altria's December 24 deadline to bid or walk away.

stories.headline: EU leaders pick Spain's Pablo Hernández de Cos to lead the ECB as Tokyo inflation hits a 16 month high.
stories.happened: At a summit that opened on November 26, EU leaders agreed to nominate Pablo Hernández de Cos, former governor of Spain's central bank and head of the Bank for International Settlements, as the next ECB president, Reuters and AFP report. He would be the first Spaniard in the job. France's Laurence Boone was nominated to run market operations and Germany's Markus Brunnermeier as chief economist. Christine Lagarde said in October she will step down on February 7, 2027.
stories.happening: The European Council will consult the European Parliament and the ECB Governing Council, then formally appoint all three at its December meeting, LB.ua reports. The same summit ended without a deal on the 2028 to 2034 EU budget, Eunews says. In Japan, Tokyo core inflation rose to 2.9% in November, a 16 month high but below the 3.0% forecast. The Bank of Japan, at 1.25%, meets December 17 to 18, and markets expect a hike to 1.5%.

could.text: A new ECB leadership seen as continuity, a likely Japanese hike and a likely US Fed hike on December 9 point to borrowing costs staying high into 2027.

you: Have a variable rate loan in euros or yen? Ask your lender how a December rate change would affect your payment.
Holding cash? Compare savings and certificate rates, which tend to rise after hikes.
Traveling to Japan? The yen is near 160 per dollar, investingLive reports, so compare card and exchange fees.
stories.watch: The Fed on December 9 and the Bank of Japan on December 17 to 18.

sources.name: The Copenhagen Post citing Reuters and AFP, Nov 27

regions.covers: China, Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Southeast Asia
regions.headline: Hong Kong tech stocks jump 6.45% after a State Council meeting on stabilizing markets.
regions.text: The Hang Seng closed up 2.11% at 22,694.77 on Friday and the Hang Seng Tech index rose 6.45% to 3,637.88, Longbridge reports. A State Council executive meeting discussed a stronger role for state backed funds and encouraging insurance and pension money into stocks. South Korea's KOSPI rose 4.2% in AP's midday count, and Japan Tobacco rose 4.5% on reports it may bid for part of Imperial Brands.
regions.you: Hold a China or Hong Kong fund? Policy driven rallies can reverse quickly; rebalance rather than chase a one day jump.

sources.name: AP via Click2Houston, Asian markets, Nov 27

regions.covers: India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, Sri Lanka
regions.headline: India's Sensex drops nearly 1,000 points as oil climbs.
regions.text: The Sensex closed down 989.33 points, or 1.17%, at 83,339.26 on Friday and the Nifty 50 fell 1.07% to 25,607.20, IANS reports. IT, private banks and autos fell most, while mid and small caps edged up. The rupee weakened about 0.5% to about 92.98 per dollar. On Thursday foreign investors were net buyers of about ₹5,843 crore, provisional data cited by The Open Press show.
regions.you: Sending money home to India? A weaker rupee means each dollar buys more; compare transfer fees as well as the rate.

regions.headline: EU leaders end a summit without a deal on the 2028 to 2034 budget.
regions.text: European Council President António Costa cancelled the second day of the summit on November 27 after talks on the next long term budget ended shortly before 1 a.m., Eunews reports. "We have not reached an agreement," Costa said, adding he still sees a possible resolution in December. Most member states asked that farm and regional funding not be cut. The same summit agreed to nominate Pablo Hernández de Cos as ECB president.
regions.you: Farm or business in the EU that relies on regional funds? Follow the December talks; budget lines for 2028 onward are still open.

sources.name: The Copenhagen Post citing Reuters and AFP, Nov 27

regions.headline: A strike on Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery kills a worker and halts some operations.
regions.text: Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry said a hostile aerial projectile hit the Jazan refinery on November 26, starting a fire and suspending some operations; one Nepali worker was killed and others were injured, Arab News reports. The Saudi led coalition said it destroyed a launch platform at Yemen's Hodeidah port. On November 24 Saudi civil defense said 11 people were wounded when a drone hit a tower in Riyadh's financial district, Al Jazeera reports.
regions.you: Traveling to Saudi Arabia? Check your government's travel advice and your airline before you go; many Riyadh flights are cancelled.

regions.covers: Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa, Egypt, Zambia
regions.headline: Zambia's central bank holds its rate at 10.75% as inflation stays in its target band.
regions.text: The Bank of Zambia kept its policy rate at 10.75% on Friday, November 27, Investing.com reports. Annual inflation rose to 6.4% in November from 6.3% in October, inside the bank's 6% to 8% target band. Governor Denny Kalyalya announced the decision, and the Monetary Policy Committee said the current policy position was appropriate.
regions.you: Borrowing or saving in kwacha? With rates on hold, lock in a fixed deposit rate if you find a good one now.

regions.headline: Brazil's Ibovespa jumps 6.07% after Lula names a bank chairman as finance minister.
regions.text: The Ibovespa closed at 176,799.84 on November 26, up 6.07%, after President Lula named Luiz Carlos Trabuco, 75, chairman of Bradesco's board, to lead the Finance Ministry from January 2027, The Rio Times reports. Banco do Brasil rose 12.6% and Bradesco 11.6%. The real strengthened about 1.2% to about 5.74 per dollar, and mid November inflation came in at 0.22%, below the 0.34% expected.
regions.you: Planning a trip to Brazil? The real strengthened again this week, so compare exchange rates and card fees before you go.

sources.name: The Rio Times, Brazil markets, Nov 26

sports.headline: MLB sues the players' union days before its labor deal expires on December 1.
sports.text: On November 25 MLB filed a complaint in federal court in New York asking it to declare that a lockout would be lawful under antitrust law, MLB.com reports. The league seeks no damages and called the suit a defensive measure. The players' union called it "completely frivolous." The labor deal expires at 11:59 p.m. ET on Tuesday, December 1.
sports.you: Buying 2027 tickets or season plans? Check the refund policy in case games are affected by a lockout.

sports.headline: Netflix is reported to lead bidding for US rights to the 2030 World Cup.
sports.text: FIFA moved its US media rights sale for the 2030 men's World Cup into a second round, and Netflix made the largest offer, Inside World Football reports, citing unnamed sources. FIFA is seeking $1.5 billion to $2 billion. For 2026, Fox paid $485 million and Telemundo $600 million. The 2030 tournament is mainly in Spain, Portugal and Morocco, with three matches in Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay.
sports.you: Watch football on streaming? Big rights deals are moving to subscription services, so budget for one more plan by 2030.

sports.headline: 1,220 players register for 66 places in the IPL 2027 auction.
sports.text: The IPL 2027 player auction is set for December 16 in Goa, with 1,220 registered players, 939 Indian and 281 from 17 other countries, competing for 66 slots, 25 of them for overseas players, National Herald reports. The ten franchises hold Rs 295.60 crore combined; Lucknow Super Giants have the biggest purse at Rs 47.45 crore. England's Ben Stokes registered at a base price of Rs 2 crore.
sports.you: Follow cricket? The auction streams live; team sponsors and broadcasters often run deals around it.

entertainment.headline: Sunrise on the Reaping leads Thanksgiving Eve with $15 million.
entertainment.text: Lionsgate's The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping took $15 million on Wednesday, November 25, and is projected to make about $85 million over the five day holiday, Variety reports. Disney's Hexed opened with $7.6 million and Universal's Focker In-Law with $5.3 million, both tracking below forecasts. The industry's five day total is projected at $210 million to $215 million.
entertainment.you: Going to the movies this weekend? Matinee and weekday tickets are usually cheaper than evening shows.

entertainment.headline: Godzilla Minus Zero passes ¥19.2 billion worldwide, beating Godzilla Minus One.
entertainment.text: Toho said Godzilla Minus Zero has grossed more than ¥19.2 billion (about $120.7 million) worldwide through November 24, ahead of Godzilla Minus One's ¥16 billion, FilmBunch reports. In Japan it drew 3.32 million admissions and more than ¥5.3 billion in its first 21 days. In the US, distributor GKIDS has taken $55.7 million, The Numbers shows.
entertainment.you: Want to see it on a big screen? Check local listings; Japanese films are getting longer international runs.

innovation.headline: The FDA approves the first new hormone therapy for early breast cancer in more than 20 years.
innovation.text: Genentech's giredestrant, sold as Wilserdly, was approved on November 23 as an after surgery treatment for stage I to III ER positive, HER2 negative breast cancer at intermediate to high risk of recurrence. In the lidERA trial of 4,170 adults it cut the risk of invasive recurrence by 30% versus standard hormone therapy, with about 92% alive and cancer free after three years versus 89.6%.
innovation.you: Being treated for early breast cancer? Ask your oncologist whether the new option fits and whether your insurer covers it.

innovation.headline: Physicists hold a single antimatter particle in its lowest quantum state for months.
innovation.text: A Northwestern team led by Gerald Gabrielse trapped one positron, the electron's antimatter twin, cooled it to about 300 millikelvin and held it for months, ScienceDaily reported on November 25. The team moved it between energy levels with microwaves. Next it plans to compare the positron's magnetism with the electron's, a test that could reveal physics beyond the Standard Model.
innovation.you: Basic research like this is decades from products; it is worth following, not investing on.

innovation.headline: The largest trial of robotic knee replacement finds no clear benefit over standard surgery.
innovation.text: The UK RACER-Knee trial, published in The Lancet, compared robotic arm assisted surgery with conventional knee replacement in 339 patients at 10 hospitals and found no meaningful difference in a key one year patient score, ScienceDaily reported on November 25. Robotic surgery added about 10.5 minutes and roughly £950 per operation and was not cost effective in year one.
innovation.you: Facing a knee replacement? Ask your surgeon about their own results; newer technology is not automatically better.

travel.headline: Lake Balaton, Hungary: a lake holiday without Como's crowds.
travel.text: Lonely Planet named Lake Balaton one of its most underrated places for 2027, for summer festivals, castles and lavender fields, as an alternative to Lake Como.
travel.you: Planning summer 2027? Look at lakeside towns now, and pay in forint rather than accepting a card conversion to dollars.

travel.headline: St. Augustine, Florida: Spanish streets without a transatlantic flight.
travel.text: Lonely Planet's 2027 underrated list includes St. Augustine for centuries of history and Spanish style streets that give a European feel on a domestic trip.
travel.you: Want old Europe on a short break? A domestic trip skips passports and long haul fares. Check the official visitor site for events before you book.

travel.headline: The dollar buys more in Argentina and Brazil than in a year.
travel.text: Argentina's peso closed at 1,580 per dollar on November 20, its weakest in at least 12 months, and Brazil's real closed near 5.93, its weakest since January 2025. Lonely Planet's 2027 list also picks Bolivia and Quito.
travel.you: Pay in the local currency when a card terminal offers dollars, and use a card with no foreign transaction fee.

picks.title: The Invisible Hand of Maria Edgeworth
picks.text: The New York Times journalist and author of Limitless profiles Maria Edgeworth, a Regency era novelist who corresponded with Thomas Malthus and David Ricardo and wove lessons on money and trade into her fiction. Named one of the New York Times Book Review's 100 Notable Books of 2026.

picks.title: Oobah: Scams for a Better Tomorrow
picks.by: Oobah Butler, directed by Daniel Lucchesi
picks.where: HBO and HBO Max, weekly from November 22
picks.text: A five episode documentary comedy in which journalist Oobah Butler tests industries from wine and wellness to dating apps by gaming online reviews and building invented brands. A practical look at how fake reviews and made up businesses can move real money.

items.text: NASA ran a developmental RS-25 Moon rocket engine for its full 200 seconds at Stennis Space Center.
Scientists found bacteria that removed about 98% of radioactive promethium-147 in 60 hours.
India declared at 720 for 9 in Wellington, the highest Test innings ever made in New Zealand.
NASA's Voyager 1 reached one light-day from Earth.
ESA and JAXA's BepiColombo entered orbit around Mercury after nearly eight years in space.
ESA's Hera is arriving at the asteroid Didymos to study the crater from NASA's DART impact.
Artemis II splashed down off San Diego after a 10 day trip around the Moon, the first crewed lunar voyage in more than 50 years.
NASA's Perseverance set the record for distance driven on another world, more than 45 km on Mars.
The Hubble Space Telescope completed its 200,000th orbit of Earth.
